Use the political cartoon to answer the question.

The cartoon, published in Harper's Weekly in 1874 by Thomas Nast, shows a White League member and a Ku Klux Klan member shaking hands over a crouching African American family. A lynched body hangs in the background, a burning schoolhouse is visible, and the caption reads 'The Union as It Was' with 'Worse Than Slavery' at the bottom.

What does the handshake between the White League member and the Ku Klux Klan member most directly represent?

choices.text: A rivalry between two competing groups for political control of Southern states
A political compromise to end military occupation of the South
An alliance between white supremacist groups using violence to oppress Black citizens
An agreement between Southern leaders to support federal Reconstruction policies

items.stem:
Use the political cartoon to answer the question.

The cartoon, published in Harper's Weekly in 1874 by Thomas Nast, shows a White League member and a Ku Klux Klan member shaking hands over a crouching African American family, with a lynched body and burning schoolhouse visible. The caption reads 'Worse Than Slavery.'

Nast's caption 'Worse Than Slavery' suggests which of the following arguments about Reconstruction?

choices.text: Legal freedom without federal protection left African Americans vulnerable to violence and oppression comparable to enslavement
Free labor was economically less productive than enslaved labor in the postwar South
Southern states had achieved greater independence after Reconstruction than before the Civil War
Many formerly enslaved people preferred the security of slavery over the uncertainties of freedom

items.stem:
Use the political cartoon to answer the question.

The cartoon, published in Harper's Weekly in 1874 by Thomas Nast, shows a White League member and a Ku Klux Klan member shaking hands over a crouching African American family. A burning schoolhouse and lynched body appear in the background. The caption reads 'Worse Than Slavery.'

Which broader historical development best explains the conditions Nast depicts in this cartoon?

choices.text: The success of Congressional Reconstruction in rebuilding Southern state governments
The collapse of federal enforcement in the South, allowing white supremacist groups to reverse Reconstruction gains
The passage of the 13th Amendment, which immediately guaranteed equal rights for all citizens
The spread of the sharecropping system, which kept formerly enslaved people in economic dependency

items.stem: Look at the word assimilation. It means to make people fit into a new culture. The Dawes Act tried to make Native Americans do what?
items.stemEs: Mira la palabra asimilación. Significa hacer que las personas se adapten a una nueva cultura. ¿La Ley Dawes trató de hacer que los nativos americanos hicieran qué?

choices.text: Form their own separate country
Leave the United States
Return to their original lands
Give up their traditions and live like white settlers
choices.textEs: Abandonar sus tradiciones y vivir como los colonos blancos

items.stem: The Dawes Act of 1887 was primarily designed to:

choices.text: Provide military protection for American Indian communities
Divide tribal lands into individual allotments to promote private land ownership
Create boarding schools for American Indian children
Establish permanent reservation boundaries for American Indian tribes to prevent further land disputes

items.stem: Which statement best describes the federal government's assimilation policy toward American Indians in the late 19th century?

choices.text: The government sought to preserve traditional American Indian languages and cultural practices on reservations
The government promoted cultural exchange between American Indians
The government aimed to eliminate American Indian cultural practices
The government focused exclusively on military conquest without attempting cultural change

items.stem:
Use the political cartoon to answer the question.

The cartoon from Puck magazine shows Theodore Roosevelt wielding a large club labeled 'Big Stick' against moneybag figures representing industrial trusts, depicting his Progressive Era antitrust policies.

What does the 'Big Stick' label on Roosevelt's club most directly symbolize?

choices.text: The labor union movement that supported Roosevelt's antitrust agenda
Presidential and federal power used to confront and regulate corporate monopolies
The U.S. military, which Roosevelt deployed against striking workers
Public outrage that pressured Congress to pass antitrust legislation

items.stem:
Use the political cartoon to answer the question.

The Puck magazine cartoon shows Theodore Roosevelt swinging a club labeled 'Big Stick' at moneybag figures representing industrial trusts during the Progressive Era.

Roosevelt's campaign against industrial trusts is best understood as a response to which of the following conditions?

choices.text: European nations forming economic alliances that threatened American trade dominance
Massive industrial monopolies that had accumulated enough power to undermine competition and corrupt government
A wave of immigration that disrupted American labor markets and industry
Small businesses calling on the federal government to protect them from foreign competitors

items.stem:
Use the political cartoon to answer the question.

The Puck magazine cartoon shows Theodore Roosevelt wielding his 'Big Stick' against industrial trusts, portraying him as a forceful reformer challenging the economic power of corporate monopolies.

Historians debate whether Roosevelt was a genuine opponent of big business or a moderate who actually preserved corporate capitalism. Which evidence from your knowledge of his presidency best supports the argument that Roosevelt's trust-busting was selective and limited?

choices.text: Roosevelt refused to pursue any antitrust cases, preferring instead to negotiate privately with corporate leaders
Roosevelt's antitrust campaign quickly lost public support because most Americans opposed government regulation of business
Roosevelt distinguished between 'good trusts' and 'bad trusts,' targeting only those he deemed harmful while leaving many large corporations intact
Congress blocked all of Roosevelt's antitrust legislation, and courts struck down the Sherman Antitrust Act during his presidency

items.stem: Sinclair's novel, from which this passage is taken, contributed most directly to the passage of which federal legislation?

choices.text: The Sherman Antitrust Act
The Pure Food and Drug Act and Meat Inspection Act
The Federal Reserve Act
The Underwood Tariff Act

items.stem: How did Booker T. Washington's approach to African American advancement differ from W.E.B. Du Bois's approach in the early 1900s?

choices.text: Washington worked with the Republican Party to pass federal civil rights legislation while Du Bois organized strikes by Black industrial workers
Washington focused on political protest and legal challenges to Jim Crow laws while Du Bois emphasized Black economic development through business ownership
Washington emphasized vocational training and economic self-reliance while accepting temporary social segregation, whereas Du Bois demanded immediate civil and political equality
Washington supported Black emigration to Africa as the only path to equality while Du Bois argued for integration within American society

items.stem: How did W.E.B. Du Bois's founding of the Niagara Movement in 1905 reflect his disagreement with Booker T. Washington's philosophy?

choices.text: The Niagara Movement focused on building Black vocational schools in the South to compete directly with Washington's Tuskegee Institute
The Niagara Movement demanded immediate political rights, civil equality, and an end to racial discrimination — rejecting Washington's policy of accommodation
The Niagara Movement supported Washington's economic self-reliance strategy but demanded that the federal government fund Black businesses
The Niagara Movement called for African Americans to emigrate to West Africa to establish an independent Black nation

items.stem: Which constitutional principle did the Supreme Court establish in Schenck v. United States?

choices.text: The federal government cannot draft citizens during wartime
All political speech is absolutely protected from federal regulation
Speech protected by the First Amendment can be limited when it creates a clear and present danger
States may not regulate any form of speech without congressional approval

items.stem: How did Germany's use of unrestricted submarine warfare help shift American public opinion toward entering World War I?

choices.text: German submarines attacked ships carrying American passengers and goods, resulting in American deaths that outraged the public
German submarines were used to deliver secret agents to American ports, threatening domestic security
German submarines destroyed a US Navy warship in the Atlantic, which constituted a formal act of war under international law
German submarines blocked American ships from trading with neutral nations, causing an economic recession

items.stem: What was the significance of the Zimmermann Telegram in drawing the United States closer to entering World War I?

choices.text: It confirmed that Britain had been secretly selling weapons to Germany, undermining US neutrality
It showed that President Wilson had been secretly negotiating a separate peace with the German government
It revealed that Germany had offered military support to Mexico in exchange for attacking the United States, alarming American leaders
It exposed a German plot to bribe US senators into blocking a declaration of war

items.stem: Which combination of factors best explains why the United States entered World War I in April 1917 rather than in 1914 when the war began?

choices.text: Wilson's re-election in 1916 on a neutrality platform, combined with escalating German provocations and the Zimmermann Telegram in early 1917, tipped the balance toward war
Germany only began using submarines in 1917, and the Zimmermann Telegram was not sent until that year
Congress passed a law in 1916 requiring a two-year waiting period before any war declaration could take effect
American public opinion immediately favored war in 1914 but Congress refused to act until European allies formally requested US assistance

items.stem: Which conclusion about the causes of the Great Depression is best supported by evidence that American agricultural prices had been declining throughout the 1920s?

choices.text: The collapse of farm prices was primarily caused by tariff policies that made American agricultural exports uncompetitive in foreign markets.
Economic problems that ultimately contributed to the Depression were present in the agricultural sector well before the 1929 stock market crash.
Agricultural decline proved that the federal government's failure to regulate farming practices was the central long-term cause of the Depression.
The international competition created by postwar European agricultural recovery was the primary driver of American farm price decline.

items.stem: Germany implemented a policy of unrestricted submarine warfare in 1917, announcing it would sink all ships — neutral or belligerent — in the war zone around Britain. Which of the following best evaluates Germany's strategic reasoning and its fatal flaw?
items.stemEs: Alemania implementó una política de guerra submarina irrestricta en 1917, anunciando que hundiría todos los barcos — neutrales o beligerantes — en la zona de guerra alrededor de Gran Bretaña. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones evalúa mejor el razonamiento estratégico de Alemania y su error fatal?

choices.text: Germany gambled that submarines could force Britain to surrender before U.S. forces mobilized — an internally coherent strategy whose fatal flaw was underestimating how quickly American troops would arrive and affect the battlefield.
choices.textEs: Alemania apostó a que los submarinos podrían obligar a Gran Bretaña a rendirse antes de que las fuerzas de EE. UU. pudieran movilizarse — una estrategia internamente coherente cuyo error fatal fue subestimar con qué rapidez llegarían las fuerzas americanas y afectarían el campo de batalla.

choices.text: Germany implemented unrestricted submarine warfare with the genuine belief that the United States would never declare war regardless of the naval provocation, since domestic isolationism would prevent Wilson from taking military action.
choices.textEs: Alemania implementó la guerra submarina irrestricta creyendo que Estados Unidos nunca declararía la guerra independientemente de la provocación.

choices.text: Germany implemented unrestricted submarine warfare and it succeeded strategically in forcing Britain to begin serious peace negotiations before the United States had time to formally declare war and begin mobilizing forces.
choices.textEs: Alemania implementó la guerra submarina irrestricta y tuvo éxito al obligar a Gran Bretaña a buscar negociaciones de paz antes de que EE. UU. declarara la guerra.

choices.text: Germany implemented unrestricted submarine warfare without any coherent strategic reasoning, acting purely out of desperation and a desire to demonstrate continued military capability after years of grueling stalemate on the Western Front.
choices.textEs: Alemania implementó la guerra submarina irrestricta sin ningún razonamiento estratégico, puramente como un acto desesperado para demostrar capacidad militar.
